q: Maya earns $40 a week. Which purchase is a need rather than a want?
o: A winter coat when hers no longer fits
A third pair of designer sneakers
e: Needs are essentials such as clothing, food and shelter.

q: A shopper keeps asking, "Do I need this or just want it?" before buying. This habit helps with what?
e: Separating needs from wants prevents overspending.

q: A person who buys on impulse and rarely checks prices has which money tendency?
e: Money personality shows habits with spending and saving.

q: Why is it useful to know your own money personality?
o: It helps you spot habits that may hurt or help your finances

q: Donating to a food bank provides which benefit?
o: It helps others in the community and may offer tax benefits
e: Charitable giving benefits both giver and community.

q: Which financial goal is SMART (specific, measurable, attainable, relevant, time-bound)?
o: Save $1,200 in 12 months by setting aside $100 each month
e: SMART goals have numbers and deadlines.

q: A goal of paying for college in ten years is an example of which type of goal?
e: Long-term goals take more than five years.

q: A reconciliation shows a $25 charge missing from your records. What should you do?
o: Find out what it was and correct your records or dispute it

q: An income statement for a month lists what?
If monthly income is $2,400 and expenses are $2,150, what is the result?
e: Income minus expenses equals surplus or deficit.

q: A budget that includes short-, medium- and long-term goals should do what?
o: Set aside money for each goal while covering essential expenses
e: Budgets turn goals into monthly actions.

q: Which budget category would an emergency fund contribution belong to?
Which is an asset?
e: Assets have value; liabilities are what you owe.

q: A net worth statement is calculated by doing what?
Assets of $18,000 and liabilities of $7,500 give a net worth of what?
A $400 car repair that was not budgeted most likely does what?
o: Reduces money available for other categories or goals

q: Which strategy helps absorb unplanned spending?
Which is an employee benefit?
A 401(k) employer match is best described as what?

q: Which payroll tax funds Social Security and Medicare?

q: Which is usually deducted from a paycheck?
Gross pay is what?
e: Net pay is gross minus deductions.

q: Gross pay is $1,000 and deductions are $230. Net pay is what?
Which is a cost of owning a home that renters usually avoid?
e: Owners pay taxes, upkeep and repairs.

q: A benefit of owning a home compared with renting is what?
o: Building equity as the loan is paid down

q: A benefit of leasing a vehicle rather than buying is what?
o: Lower monthly payments, but no ownership at the end
e: Leases often have mileage limits and no equity.

q: Buying a car and keeping it for years is often cheaper in the long run because what?
o: Payments end and you keep the vehicle

q: Rent-to-own arrangements usually cost more than paying cash because what?
o: Total payments include high fees and markups
e: Compare total cost, not just weekly payments.

q: Which payment method usually has the highest total cost for the same item?
o: Store credit with a high interest rate carried for months

q: Which strategy helps a consumer make a smart purchase?
o: Comparing unit prices and reading reviews

q: A 12-ounce box costs $3.00 and a 20-ounce box costs $4.60. Which is the better unit price?
A good short-term saving goal is to do what?
o: Build an emergency fund covering several months of expenses

q: Where is an emergency fund best kept?
o: In an easily accessible savings account

q: Saving for a house down payment in five years is an example of what?
e: Goals of several years are intermediate-term.

q: For a goal five years away, a moderate mix of savings and lower-risk investments is common because what?
o: There is time to earn returns but limited time to recover from losses

q: A charitable contribution to a qualified nonprofit may do what on a tax return?
o: Reduce taxable income if deductions are itemized

q: To claim a charitable deduction, a donor should keep what?
A long-term investing strategy for retirement should emphasize what?
Which account type offers tax advantages for retirement saving?
Banks and credit unions help savers by doing what?
o: Holding deposits safely and paying interest
e: Financial institutions channel savings to borrowers.

q: The stock market allows investors to do what?
o: Buy and sell ownership shares in companies

q: Compound growth means that interest is earned on what?
o: Both the original deposit and previously earned interest

q: $1,000 grows at 5 percent compounded annually. After one year the balance is $1,050. After the second year it is closest to what?
Compared with a checking account, a savings account usually offers what?
o: Higher interest but limits on withdrawals

q: Stocks generally offer which risk-return trade-off compared with bonds?
o: Higher potential return with greater risk

q: A mutual fund helps investors by doing what?
o: Pooling money to buy a diversified mix of investments

q: Which is a cost people face in retirement?
o: Health care and possible long-term care

q: Many retirees need money for which basic expense?
Which is a common source of retirement income?
e: Social Security replaces part of earnings.

q: A pension is best described as what?
o: A regular payment from an employer plan after retirement

q: Starting to save for retirement at 25 instead of 45 helps because of what?
o: Compound growth has more years to work

q: Saving a sufficient percentage of income each year matters because what?
o: Small amounts may not fund retirement needs

q: Which source of credit is generally the most expensive?
e: Payday loans have very high APRs.

q: A title loan requires a borrower to do what?
o: Use a vehicle title as collateral
e: Failure to repay can mean losing the vehicle.

q: Revolving credit, such as a credit card, allows a borrower to do what?
o: Borrow repeatedly up to a limit

q: An auto loan with equal monthly payments for 60 months is what type of credit?
Taking on a $350 monthly loan payment affects a budget by doing what?
o: Reducing the money available for other expenses and goals
e: Debt payments are a fixed expense.

q: Borrowing to buy a depreciating item can do what to net worth?
o: Lower it, because liabilities may exceed asset value

q: Which of the three Cs of credit refers to a borrower's reliability and history of repaying?
e: Lenders consider character, capacity and collateral.

q: Capacity in credit evaluation means what?
o: The borrower's ability to repay from income

q: Consumers can get a free credit report from the three major credit bureaus at what site?
A credit score is best described as what?
o: A number summarizing how risky a borrower appears

q: Why check credit reports regularly?
o: To catch errors and signs of identity theft

q: If you find an error on a credit report, you should do what?
o: Dispute it with the credit bureau in writing

q: Which event could lead to bankruptcy?
o: Large unpaid medical bills after job loss
e: Unexpected hardship plus debt can overwhelm a household.

q: Bankruptcy is a legal process in which what happens?
o: A person seeks relief from debts they cannot repay

q: Paying bills 30 days late repeatedly will most likely do what?
e: Payment history is a key factor.

q: A consequence of poor credit management can be what?
o: Higher interest rates and difficulty renting or getting loans

q: APR stands for what?
A fixed interest rate on a loan does what?
o: Stays the same for the life of the loan

q: A larger down payment reduces the total cost of borrowing because what?
o: Less money is borrowed, so less interest accrues

q: Making extra payments toward principal helps by doing what?
o: Reducing interest costs and paying off the loan sooner

q: A debit card differs from a credit card in that a debit card does what?
o: Withdraws money directly from your bank account

q: Carrying a balance on a credit card leads to what?
o: Interest charges added to what you owe

q: Financial risk can be defined as what?
o: The possible loss of assets or earning potential

q: Which event is a financial risk?
Buying insurance to protect against a major loss is an example of which risk strategy?

q: Choosing not to take a dangerous activity is what risk strategy?

o: The amount paid before coverage starts
The maximum amount the insurer will pay for a covered loss
e: Higher deductibles often mean lower premiums.

q: Employer-sponsored health insurance often costs less than individual coverage because what?
o: Employers usually share part of the premium

q: Disability insurance protects against what?
o: Loss of income if you cannot work due to illness or injury

q: Term life insurance differs from whole life insurance in that term insurance does what?
o: Covers a set period and usually costs less

q: Life insurance is most important for people who do what?
o: Have dependents who rely on their income

q: Renter's insurance generally covers what?
Homeowner's insurance generally covers what?
o: Damage to the home and personal property from covered events

q: Which factor can raise the price of automobile insurance?
o: A history of accidents or tickets

q: An extended warranty is best described as what?
o: Optional coverage that may not be worth its cost
e: Compare the cost with likely repairs.

q: Mortgage insurance is usually required when a buyer does what?
Which action helps prevent identity theft?

o: Is long, unique and hard to guess

q: An email that urges you to click a link and confirm your bank password is most likely what?
e: Phishing tricks people into giving information.

q: A pyramid scheme earns money mainly by doing what?
o: Recruiting new participants who pay in

q: The Better Business Bureau helps consumers by doing what?
o: Providing business ratings and handling complaints
e: Consumer protection agencies help resolve disputes.

q: Which agency regulates consumer financial products like credit cards and mortgages?
A will is a legal document that does what?
o: Directs how your property is distributed after death
e: Wills also name guardians for minor children.

q: A beneficiary designation on a retirement account does what?
o: Names who receives the account after the owner dies

q: A power of attorney allows someone to do what?
o: Act on your behalf in legal or financial matters

q: A living will states what?
o: Your wishes for medical treatment if you cannot speak for yourself

q: On average, higher levels of education are associated with what?

Which is a direct cost of college?
e: Costs include books, housing and food.

q: Opportunity cost of attending college full time includes what?
o: Income you could have earned by working
e: Foregone wages are a real cost.

q: Which type of institution usually has the lowest tuition for in-state students?
e: Public two-year schools are lower cost.

q: Why may a private university cost more than a public one?
o: It receives less state funding and relies more on tuition

q: Which measure helps evaluate the quality of a college investment?
o: Graduation rate and job placement outcomes

q: A school with a very low graduation rate and high debt for students is likely to be what?
When is it best to submit the FAFSA?
o: As early as possible after it opens
e: Some aid is limited and first-come.

q: Which is a source of funds for college that does not need to be repaid?
Work-study programs help students by doing what?
o: Providing part-time jobs to earn money for school

q: A disadvantage of student loans is that they must be what?
An advantage of grants over loans is that grants do what?
o: Do not have to be repaid
